functional.text: Purchase: the customer selects a slot code; if the balance covers the price and the slot is in stock, the product is dispensed.
Accept coins and notes of fixed denominations, rejecting anything else; keep a running balance across several insertions.
Return exact change after a sale; cancel refunds the whole balance; refuse the sale if exact change is impossible.
Sold-out slots refuse selection without taking money; an operator restocks slots and refills/empties the coin box in maintenance mode.

non_functional.text: Behaviour per mode is easy to read and to extend (new modes, card payment) without editing every method.
Money is never lost: every path ends in a dispensed product plus change, or a full refund.

assumptions.text: ~30 slots × 10 items, one product and price per slot.
One customer at a time; maintenance blocks sales.

out_of_scope.text: Card payment (designed for, not built), telemetry to a fleet backend.

api.notes: Errors: SoldOut, InsufficientFunds, NoExactChange (money kept as balance or refunded).
Returns the full balance; machine goes back to Idle.

deep_dives.title: Organising mode-dependent behaviour

options.name: mode enum + if/else in each method
options.cons: every new mode touches every method; illegal transitions are easy

options.name: State pattern
options.pros: one class per mode, transitions explicit

deep_dives.choice: State pattern: MachineState interface with IdleState, HasMoneyState, DispensingState, MaintenanceState
deep_dives.why: Each state handles every event and sets the next state on the machine; adding Maintenance (or a CardAuthorising state) adds a class instead of editing a switch in four methods.

deep_dives.title: Making change

options.name: greedy largest coin first
options.pros: simple, optimal for unlimited US coins
options.cons: fails with a limited coin box

options.name: bounded DP over available coins
options.pros: finds a combination whenever one exists

deep_dives.choice: ChangeMaker: greedy first, bounded DP fallback over the coin box counts
deep_dives.why: The coin box is finite; we must know before dispensing whether exact change is possible, otherwise refuse and refund.

wrapup.bottlenecks: None at runtime; the risky piece is change making with a near-empty coin box.
wrapup.failures: Dispense motor jams → refund and mark the slot faulty; no exact change → refuse the sale and keep or refund the balance; power loss → persist balance and resume in HasMoney.
wrapup.monitoring: Sales and sold-out events per slot, coin box levels, refusals for no change.
wrapup.scale: A new payment method is a PaymentMethod implementation plus possibly a new state; a new product type needs no change.
wrapup.future: Card payment via a PaymentMethod interface and a CardAuthorising state; remote stock telemetry.
